title: A Field for Tomorrow
old_p1: An army from Babylon was all around Jerusalem, and Jeremiah was kept in the guards’ courtyard. It was a very hard time, and soon the army would take the land.
Heavenly Father told Jeremiah, “Your cousin Hanameel will come and ask you to buy his field.” A field is land where food grows. Soon Hanameel came, just as Heavenly Father said.
old_p2: Jeremiah weighed out seventeen pieces of silver to pay. He signed the paper, sealed it shut, and had people watch so everyone knew it was true.
His helper Baruch put the paper in a clay jar so it would last many days. Why? Heavenly Father promised that someday people would own houses and fields here again.
Buying the field was a way to show hope. When tomorrow feels hard, you can do one hopeful thing today, like planting a seed.
p1: An army from Babylon was all around Jerusalem. The prophet Jeremiah was shut in the prison yard.
Heavenly Father told Jeremiah, “Your cousin Hanameel will ask you to buy his field.” A field is land where food can grow. Then Hanameel came, just as Heavenly Father said.
Jeremiah paid seventeen pieces of silver for the field. He signed a paper that said the field was his. People watched, so everyone knew it was true.
p2: Jeremiah asked his helper Baruch to keep the paper safe in a clay jar. Why buy a field when an army was coming? Heavenly Father promised His people would live in that land again.
Buying the field showed that Jeremiah had hope. Hope means believing good things are coming. Tonight, tell Heavenly Father one good thing you hope for tomorrow.
